title: Book Two · Chapter 85: The Paid Return
story:
In the middle of winter, Dad comes home with an envelope. It has no money inside, only a signed paper. He puts it beside his work bag before he washes.

Ronan sees the folded edge. He does not open it.

“Is that a payment?” he asks when Dad returns.

“A return of part of an old payment. I finished paying it back today.”

“For the door in your old book?”

Dad nods. “That one.”

Ronan looks at the envelope. He remembers the second visit and the extra part. The customer waited for money too, not only for a working door.

“Is the person happy now?”

“I cannot tell you that. He signed for the money. The door works, and that part of the payment is returned.”

“Will he ask you again?”

“Perhaps not.”

Ronan sits down. Dad finished the payment. Ronan wants that to make everything good again. But the customer may not come back. He does not like that thought.

Mum brings her notebook. They check the household money before supper. Dad gives her the amount from this week's work. The old return is already on their plan. Mum draws a short line beside it.

“Less to pay back next month,” she says.

Dad lets out a breath. “Yes.”

Dad's voice is softer now. Dad is not smiling widely, but his shoulders drop. Mum touches his arm. Then she puts the notebook away.

Dad puts the envelope away. He keeps it with the old shop book. It does not go on the kitchen wall. It stays out of Ronan's school folder too.

After supper, Dad asks Ronan to hold one side of a cloth. They are cleaning the top of a low cupboard. There are no tools and no new repair. Ronan wipes the near side. Dad reaches the back.

A little wooden bead rolls out from behind a cup. Ronan catches it before it falls.

“Treasure,” he says.

Dad takes a look. “A very small treasure.”

They ask Mum about it. It is from an old sewing job. The owner left the spare pieces with her. She lets Ronan keep it.

He threads it onto a short piece of string. It looks too small for a necklace and too large for a button. He ties it to his pencil case instead.

At bedtime, he turns it between his fingers. Dad comes to the door and says good night. Ronan asks if they can play at the square on Sunday.

“If it stays dry,” Dad says.

Ronan puts the pencil case down and looks out at the clear patch of sky.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

return＝返还；payment＝付款；envelope＝信封。

## 理解问题

1. Dad为什么收到旧客户的签字？
2. Ronan怎样理解还钱后的余下责任？

## 读句子

**Dad / puts / the envelope away.** Dad／收好／信封。
